items.q: Why is user count the wrong capacity plan?
items.a: One action can start many model calls, and each call can be huge. Their examples: 1 call for a chatbot turn, 10–20 for a copilot, ~50 for a research agent, thousands for an autonomous job. Requests in their fleet run from ~50 tokens to ~100,000. Those are examples, not a sizing formula.

items.q: How can a router make the fleet look out of GPUs?
items.a: Routing picks the cache. The hit rate picks the batch. The batch picks utilization. The autoscaler reads utilization. A capacity scare can start several hops away from the card.

items.q: Why is retry the wrong fix after 200 tokens?
items.a: The user already has them. Preempting the GPU mid-stream does not say what to do with output already shown. A cold spare is not capacity until it is warm, and the KV cache does not come along for free.

items.q: What should the optimization be measured against?
items.a: Cost per successful task. Avoid, share, move, or delay the work. Cost per token can fall while step three of five aborts the spend from steps one and two.

items.q: What is the inference control plane?
items.a: The layer that picks the model, the batch, the cache, and the recovery together. Same GPUs, different scheduling, different result. Adding cards can hide a bad scheduler. Captions are missing; this is the conference page's reconstruction.
